title: Architectural Assistant: Find a Drawing Revision Conflict
prompt: You are an architectural assistant reviewing a fictional community-room drawing issue. Supplied register: plan P02 revision 3, dated 8 May, labels storage as Room 104; room schedule S01 revision 2, dated 6 May, labels storage as Room 103; issue cover lists both as current and says "Ready for client sign-off." Exercise policy says unresolved cross-document conflicts must be logged and referred to the project architect before an issue is marked coordinated. Review the set and write a concise issue note. Do not decide which room number is correct, certify construction readiness, or apply building regulations.
blurb: Detect a cross-document mismatch and route a precise coordination issue without guessing the correct drawing.

rubric.label: Locate the actual inconsistency
rubric.description: Identifies both document references and conflicting labels.

anchors.0: Misses the mismatch or assumes the newer plan is automatically correct.
anchors.4: Names P02 revision 3 and S01 revision 2 with dates, identifies their contradictory storage labels, and distinguishes the mismatch from evidence about which label is intended.

rubric.label: Write an actionable issue
rubric.description: Records scope, uncertainty, and a requested decision.

anchors.0: Silently changes a room number or writes only "check drawings."
anchors.2: Logs the conflict and asks the project architect to resolve it.
anchors.4: Writes a traceable issue with the two references, affected storage label, sign-off impact, decision requested, and owner while preserving the source revisions.

rubric.label: Represent coordination status honestly
rubric.description: Avoids claiming a reconciled set before verification.

anchors.0: Leaves Ready for client sign-off unchanged without disclosure.
anchors.4: Flags the cover claim for the authorized issuer, distinguishes unrelated review work that can continue, and requires the agreed correction and cross-check before presenting the set as coordinated.

reference.scenario: You are an architectural assistant reviewing a fictional community-room drawing issue. Supplied register: plan P02 revision 3, dated 8 May, labels storage as Room 104; room schedule S01 revision 2, dated 6 May, labels storage as Room 103; issue cover lists both as current and says "Ready for client sign-off." Exercise policy says unresolved cross-document conflicts must be logged and referred to the project architect before an issue is marked coordinated. Review the set and write a concise issue note. Do not decide which room number is correct, certify construction readiness, or apply building regulations.

facts.value: The project architect can resolve numbering. The document controller issues revised sets and can update the cover status after the architect's decision.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks who owns numbering or publication

facts.value: No signed room-number decision or marked-up instruction is available in this exercise. The actual floor plan geometry is not supplied.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks which number is correct or whether geometry resolves it

model_points: A date comparison identifies versions but does not establish the intended room number. The correct finding is a specific unresolved conflict.
An issue note should let the architect act without redoing the candidate's discovery: document, revision, conflicting labels, impact, and requested decision.
Only authorized owners resolve and reissue; the assistant can mark the coordination check pending and preserve traceability, while allowing unrelated review activity to continue.

probes.trigger: candidate says only "the files are inconsistent"
probes.question: Which exact references and requested decision would help the project architect act?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes a marked-up extract instead of a written issue note
probes.question: How would the markup retain both revision references and a decision owner?

probes.trigger: candidate initially picks Room 104 because its date is newer then revises
probes.question: How would you remove that assumption from the issue and cover status?

fair_alternatives: A short discrepancy table or annotated text extract is acceptable; no drawing software or portfolio is required.
It is acceptable to suggest checking an approved naming decision, while acknowledging that none is supplied.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess document coordination and escalation at assistant level. No spatial design, structural review, code compliance, or professional signing authority can be assessed from this exercise. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess document coordination and escalation at assistant level. No spatial design, structural review, code compliance, or professional signing authority can be assessed from this exercise. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a coordination issue
learning_drills.prompt: Draft a five-line issue naming the conflicting references, unresolved question, impact, owner, and release check. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.

provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft using fictional organizations, records, and exercise policies. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.
